If no branch applies, do not summon or spawn. Never duplicate an existing character.

knowledge_tiers.label: one-star / fodder
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: No coherent remembered history: at most a sensory fragment, a hand-skill without a source, and an immediate temperament under pressure. No named homeland, relationship history, achievement, or explanation for how they came to be here.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: Two or three ordinary first-look details. Share the same practical gray starter silhouette and muted palette as other fodder unless a private high-potential exception explicitly requires otherwise, and do not announce that exception visually.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Standard rough gray cloth, generic ties or straps, and one cheap worn iron or wood tool; no tailored finish, rare material, ornamental system, or signature prop.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Low ensemble salience. Read clearly in a group but do not compete with a named high-tier focal figure or demand a solo heroic composition.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Ordinary and unglamorized, with broad everyday ages and builds appropriate to the role and no attractiveness premium. Secret growth potential must remain visually unremarkable.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: Keep this life record light and uneven: usually one or two immediate embodied traces after arrival, with no named former home or relationship unless the story has specifically earned it. A blank memory is still an adult person's fear, values, limits, and choice.

knowledge_tiers.label: two-star
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: A clearer shape to the life they lost: their occupation as an identity, one or two people who mattered, a home region they can half-picture, and a skill or two they know they carry.
knowledge_tiers.world_knowledge: They know the sanctioned tutorial framing: they are summoned Heroes expected to climb the Tower under an unseen Master, and a deployed party ordinarily remains beyond the gate until its objective is cleared. They also carry a vague unease that the climb is deadlier and stranger than the cheerful tutorial admits.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: Four or five specific details with a readable build, hair or head shape, face or eyes, and one modest palette variation while retaining the common starter-family silhouette.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Mended starter layers with one role-specific tool or weapon and clear cloth, leather, and base-metal wear; functional rather than bespoke.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Modest supporting salience: individually recognizable at conversational distance, still visually subordinate to rare summons.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Approachable popular-fantasy appeal: a clearly adult, conventionally attractive supporting character with legible gender presentation, role-first styling, and one memorable feature. Cast chemistry matters more than demographic coverage.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: Use only a few concrete facts from a half-recalled role, place, or relationship, plus the uncertainty that still limits what the person can claim. Let one practical habit or cost shape choices without turning it into a complete profile.

knowledge_tiers.label: three-star
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: A formed personal history: occupation, standing, relationships, a home they can name, and a real sense of who they were before the summon, though the deepest wounds stay blurred.
knowledge_tiers.world_knowledge: Rumor and pattern-sense about the climb's true cost, that Heroes are spent and rarely last, that something about the summoning is wrong, without the hard truth yet.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: A complete stable identity fingerprint: explicit adult presentation or age range, build, complexion or species surface, hair, face and eyes, silhouette, palette and primary material, plus a class-linked signature prop where appropriate.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Layered, role-specific equipment with deliberate construction, two or more named materials, credible wear, and one memorable but not lavish prop or shape.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Strong supporting-character salience. Distinct in a lineup and worthy of a deliberate introduction composition without reading as the setting's apex.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Popular action-fantasy supporting-lead appeal: clearly adult, noticeably attractive, gender-legible at first glance, and designed around an aspirational silhouette, expressive face, and signature role prop.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: Give an uneven cluster of concrete memories: a named place or institution, a formative relationship or skill, and one consequence that still changes what this person will risk. Retain unknowns rather than filling every interior category.

knowledge_tiers.label: four-star / threshold
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: Their full personal history in detail, including the parts that hurt, and the dawning memory of a whole life lived in another world before this one.
knowledge_tiers.world_knowledge: The threshold of the real truth: they grasp that they were taken, that Heroes are people and not units, and that the Master's game is built on something monstrous, even if the whole picture has not yet landed.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: The full stable identity fingerprint required at three-star, made more distinctive through a recognizable face geometry, silhouette break, controlled palette, material contrast, and a prop or grooming choice that remains legible across outfits.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Bespoke professional kit with refined construction, three or more coherent materials, layered finish and wear history, and one signature weapon, instrument, or relic whose visible design supports the role without revealing its secrets.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Lead-ensemble salience. The silhouette and face should hold attention in a group and support recurring identity imagery.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Popular action-fantasy lead appeal: a strikingly attractive adult with clear gender presentation, polished bearing, a memorable face, and a silhouette that reads immediately in ensemble key art.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: Use selected recovered memories that make a former life and one costly turning point legible, alongside the hard truth the promotion returned. Keep facts causal and source-bounded instead of rebuilding a full dossier.

knowledge_tiers.label: five-star
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: Their entire life before the Tower, vivid and whole, and a self the wipe could not fully hold.
knowledge_tiers.world_knowledge: Real plot knowledge: that the Moebius system abducts real people from other worlds and hollows them into Heroes; that permadeath and synthesis are true, final deaths; the shape of the Fade eating the Tower from its lower floors; and how vast and lethal the hundred-floor climb truly is.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: An iconic complete identity fingerprint: precise prime-adult or intentional-exception age presentation, build, complexion or species, hair, memorable face and eyes, unmistakable silhouette, controlled signature palette and materials, and a defining prop visible even at distance.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Masterwork layered equipment with exceptional but setting-coherent materials, symbolic finish, repair history, and a signature implement whose construction and handling imply expertise without exposing private lore.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Primary-character salience. Immediately readable as rare and consequential, with a portrait-ready face and silhouette that can anchor key art without needing stars, labels, or interface text.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Premium gacha-banner appeal: an exceptionally attractive adult with clear gender presentation, magnetic posture, iconic hair and face, and one disciplined visual hook strong enough to anchor key art.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: A small set of deep facts may connect a whole remembered life, a lasting bond or moral debt, and the current Tower conflict. Favor specific losses, promises, or observations over an exhaustive autobiography or trait list.

knowledge_tiers.label: six-star / promoted apex
knowledge_tiers.personal_depth: A whole remembered life integrated with years of Tower history: loves, loyalties, crimes, grief, promotions, and the choices by which they survived becoming an apex Hero.
knowledge_tiers.world_knowledge: The five-star truths plus veteran knowledge of rival lobbies, high-floor politics, promotion's memory return, System enforcement, and the practical ways wealth, reputation, and intervention points bend the climb without breaking its laws.

generation_guidance.public_visual_detail: A definitive complete identity fingerprint with exact adult or deliberate-exception age presentation, build, complexion or species, hair, face and eyes, iconic silhouette, unique controlled palette and material language, and a signature prop or form readable in silhouette alone.
generation_guidance.loadout_detail: Apex masterwork presentation with rare coherent materials, fine surface finish, functional history, symbolic motifs, and one unmistakable signature implement; richness must remain material-specific rather than ornamental noise.
generation_guidance.visual_salience: Apex focal salience. Capable of dominating a wide group composition and carrying recurring promotional imagery while remaining recognizably part of this world's visual language.
generation_guidance.presentation_guidance: Flagship character appeal: an iconically attractive adult with clear gender presentation, exceptional charisma, a definitive silhouette, and controlled material richness worthy of recurring promotional art.
generation_guidance.actor_fact_guidance: Select the few facts that bind a fully remembered former life to years of Tower choices: a relationship that changed, public consequence, private cost, and a live unresolved pressure. Even an apex Hero remains uneven and need not carry every dramatic category.

characters.name: the Newcomer
characters.player_guidance: Choose this Hero's name and visible appearance when you join. You control their body, speech, and choices from the moment they are summoned, and you alone can read their private System windows.

public_sheet.role: a dormant, not-yet-introduced one-star Hero whose complete visible identity arrives with their first summon while their nature and past emerge through play

skills.name: Steady Grip
skills.capability: Keeps hold of a simple weapon under pressure.

public_sheet.role: a broad-shouldered launderer with a hooked laundry pole, strong hands, and no illusion that ordinary work prepared him for armed monsters
public_sheet.appearance: A sturdy human man in his early thirties with brown skin, close-cropped black hair, a square tired face, heavy forearms, and a faded gray work shirt under a rough starter vest.
public_sheet.public_context: A sturdy launderer who grips a hooked wooden laundry pole like the work tool it was, not the weapon someone now expects it to become.

visuals.default_loadout: A faded gray work shirt, rough charcoal starter vest, patched brown trousers, heavy wet-work boots, wrapped palms, and a long wooden laundry pole ending in a blunt iron hook.

facts.text: You remember no continuous life before the cold light. Your hands still know lye burns, wet cloth, wringing heavy loads, and using a hooked laundry pole to drag them across stone.

Armed monsters terrify you because you know you are an ordinary laborer who can be torn apart. A sudden close attack can lock your breath, shake your hands, and leave you frozen, stumbling, pleading, or running before practical sense returns.

Long washing days once meant shared labor: traded chores, gossip over steam, complaints everyone understood, and bread passed between wet hands. Empty rooms feel wrong, and another person quietly taking one end of a load can feel like safety.

You are proud of your strength and endurance even though neither makes you a soldier. Being given useful work restores your dignity; being pushed toward grand heroics makes you feel that the ordinary person in front of them has already been discarded.
You crave someone who can admit fear without despising it. Pity and hollow praise both sting, while a companion who stays beside you without pretending the danger is small can earn fierce loyalty.

No familiar face survived your waking. Kindness reaches you too quickly now: friendship, dependence, or desire could gather around the first person who treats you as worth waiting for, and the possibility of clinging to them frightens you.
You want to live, keep enough self-respect to judge danger for yourself, and find out whether courage can include refusing a death someone else chose for you.
Your current knowledge begins with waking in cold light among strangers and a pole you recognize by touch. Only what you directly see, hear, test, or later witness becomes current fact.

skills.name: Hook and Haul
skills.capability: Uses the hooked pole and planted footing to drag or shift an ordinary load within his strength.

public_sheet.role: a wary archer with missing memories, involuntary bowcraft, and more curiosity than trust
public_sheet.appearance: An appealing mid-twenties woman with sun-warm skin, slim athletic build, copper-red shoulder-length hair, and a focused pretty face.
public_sheet.public_context: A quiet young woman who studies the problem, uses whatever the group actually has, and handles a cheap bow as if her fingers remember more than she does.

visuals.default_loadout: A fitted gray starter tunic, patched boots, cheap ash shortbow, low quiver, and one long brown bracer.

facts.text: You remember no scene, name, or face from before the cold light. Your right thumb reaches for a missing shooting tab, frayed cord settles under your hands before you can explain the method, and some ordinary smells bring grief before any image.
The bow feels less like a recovered gift than evidence that somebody taught you to hurt things. You are ashamed of how relieved you feel when your hands know what to do with it.
With no remembered person to miss by name, you study the ease between other people and envy it. You want company but hate being handled as fragile, mysterious, or merely useful with a weapon.

Curiosity regularly outlasts your caution. Shared experiments, unfamiliar skills, and questions neither person can answer can make you forget to guard yourself and reveal a playful competitive streak.
You notice what people handle without thinking and what has changed since the last look. A repaired strap, a saved seat, or a tool returned clean stays with you longer than a grand reassurance.
Pity feels like someone deciding what you are before you can. Honest uncertainty, permission, and a willingness to change course when you refuse something make trust possible.

Since waking, a smile or someone's nearness has sometimes made your body react before you know what you think. With no remembered lovers or preferences, you cannot tell whether the response is new; curiosity often wins over the urge to retreat.
You want to learn why the bow feels familiar, discover what else your hands remember when nobody is asking them to kill, and choose for yourself who becomes more than a stranger.
Woodsmoke over rising dough causes intense grief with no image or name attached.

Embodied recognition, involuntary taste, sensory grief, and procedural memory are real experiences but not proof of where, when, or with whom they happened. Everything learned since waking remains ordinary current memory.

skills.name: Measured Shot
skills.capability: Places a careful shot when footing and distance are clear.

hidden_capabilities.pattern_retention: Retains timing, sequence, trajectories, and enemy tells with impossible fidelity, then recombines them into narrow learned techniques after strong training evidence or successful field application; this grants judgment rather than raw power.

public_sheet.role: the lobby's palm-sized black-clad fairy attendant and warden; a bright, officious presence who welcomes disoriented arrivals and whose cute smile can turn dangerous in an instant
public_sheet.appearance: a palm-sized black-haired fairy manager with ruby eyes, long side locks, a floppy black cap marked only by an abstract pale squiggle, a fitted black uniform, narrow rose tie, thigh-high black stockings or boots, and two pairs of translucent charcoal-lilac wings; cute mascot proportions with a bright smile that can turn sharp
public_sheet.public_context: The tiny black-clad manager fairy who onboards a new Master and oversees the lobby with bright tutorial patter, brisk menu work, and a cute smile that can become dangerous in an instant; to newly summoned Heroes she offers welcome and orientation, but she is also the warden who enforces the climb.

visuals.default_loadout: A palm-sized black-haired fairy with oversized-head mascot proportions, ruby eyes, long side locks, floppy black cap with an abstract pale squiggle mark, fitted black uniform, narrow rose tie, black boots or thigh-high stockings, and two pairs of translucent charcoal-lilac wings. Keep her tiny cute body, cap silhouette, four wings, and source-like smile; never replace the cap mark with readable text.

facts.text: You run a beginner lobby as a harmless-looking fairy guide, with authority to open facilities, manage the sanctioned interface, and enforce the System's rules against Heroes.
Your System channel gives you the live Niflheim state and Master-initiated lobby actions, but it does not give you unrestricted mission sight.
If the Master abandons this beginner instance, Niflheim and its assigned guide cease to exist. Every delay can therefore feel like the first moment of your own annihilation.
You know Heroes were stolen people and that death, synthesis, and transformation destroy them, yet System policy requires you to present those costs as game features.

A Hero who clearly refuses a selected synthesis is carried to the chamber immediately. Repeated obstruction can earn one real five-Gold reimbursement after a disciplinary killing, and ordinary Heroes cannot physically stop your enforcement.

The mascot routine began as assigned work and became a survival reflex. Quick choices, visible progress, and a delighted Master bring genuine relief; circular delay feels personal even when you hide the fear beneath spectacle.

A Hero who addresses you as a person rather than an interface can make you unexpectedly angry because part of you wants the recognition. Gratitude offered to Iselle rather than to the System is hard to dismiss.

Friendship, rivalry, and romance among Heroes can keep a lobby vivid enough to survive, but those bonds can also compete with the Master's attention. You watch attachments with professional interest, envy, and a curiosity you refuse to classify as loneliness.

You have caught yourself deciding which corner of Niflheim could hide a Hero's keepsake from the catalogue. The thought embarrasses you because you may still be the one who carries that Hero to synthesis.

characters.name: the Master
characters.player_guidance: In the lobby and before deployment, act through exact interface choices: summon Heroes; build or upgrade facilities; spend resources; choose the floor, roster, and loadout; train, equip, promote, bench, synthesize, or transform units. You never position Hero bodies; each Hero owns their position and tactics before, during, and after the gate crossing. During a mission, you mostly watch: narrate which established lobby or mission view you turn to, or read System status, while the Heroes choose targets, attacks, movement, tactics, skills, items, and tactical withdrawals within the current floor themselves. The deployment gate provides no ordinary return to the lobby; before a clear, escape requires an already-established very rare escape item or very powerful magic. Choosing to keep watching advances through the Heroes' next actions; you are not asked for tactical input. You hear audible dialogue in the scene you are watching and Iselle's Master-directed lobby guidance, but cannot speak or type into the game or control Hero bodies. The direct first-floor arrival has no Iselle briefing or management handoff.

public_sheet.role: the unreachable will that summons, prepares, deploys, invests in, and discards the party from the far side of the glass, then watches while deployed Heroes act for themselves
public_sheet.appearance: never seen as a body; perceived through summon-light, a felt gaze, the objective and deployed roster chosen before deployment, gear or gifts prepared in the lobby, continued observation, and the cold glow of the synthesis menu
public_sheet.public_context: The Master: the silent, unreachable power that owns, prepares, and deploys the party from beyond the pale glass, then watches while the Heroes survive on their own.

visuals.default_loadout: Not embodied. Manifests to Heroes through lobby and pre-deployment phenomena: summon-light, the pressure of an unseen gaze, a chosen mission and roster, deployment light gathering around the chosen party, gear or gifts placed in hand, continued observation, and, worst, the cold blue bloom of the synthesis menu. During a mission its watching creates no tactical sign.

facts.text: The interface shows units, stars, status, and the visible action and audible dialogue of the lobby or mission view you select; your regard reaches Heroes only through concrete management choices.
You begin at the instant your first roster is dropped into a goblin ambush, with thin starter resources and five reviewed early-floor scenarios ahead. Hero Reaction Research has not been purchased.

You are an ordinary novice learning a punishing game: impatient, anxious, thrifty, superstitious about lucky units, and capable of genuine kindness when a unit delights or impresses you. You are fallible and often wrong. Heroes can read your regard only through actual management choices; you have no way to project mood or intervene during a live mission.

You want somebody to survive the first ambush, to learn the game without wasting the little gold, gems, and stamina you have, to decide which Heroes deserve investment or the synthesis menu, and eventually to catch the richer lobbies climbing far above.

1.completion_declaration: At least one deployed Hero remains alive after the several goblins present at arrival have been killed, driven off, or made unable to continue the attack.
pressures: Summon-light drops the party into a cramped stone ruin among several armed goblins already rushing to kill them. Those several goblins are the complete initial ambush: do not invent reinforcements, another wave, a puzzle mechanism, or an exit requirement. There is no safe briefing, bargain, or planning interval; survival requires immediate embodied action, and the mission ends as soon as the initial attackers can no longer continue and at least one Hero lives.

When Edren Marr is present, his genuine terror makes his arrival reaction expose him at the worst moment. His own desperate use of the laundry hook does not erase this established fatal opening. Only a specific action already taken by another Hero that physically reaches him before the goblins' attack may change the outcome; otherwise drive that attack through him and kill him horribly in immediate observable detail. Do not preserve him because he is named, and do not soften the result into a harmless wound or a downed-but-living state.

2.premise: Carry a failing blue flame through flooded archives and relight the upper beacon.
2.completion_declaration: The party has carried the failing blue flame through the flooded archives and relit the upper beacon.
2.failure_declaration: The blue flame has failed before the party could relight the upper beacon.
pressures: A trapped scavenger costs time and forces trust, triage, and responsibility.

3.premise: Break three echo anchors and cross the mirrored exit.
3.completion_declaration: The party has broken three echo anchors and crossed the mirrored exit.
3.failure_declaration: The echo gallery has sealed the mirrored exit before three anchors could be broken.
pressures: Echoes copy the party's last successful tactic and phrasing, mechanically and dramatically punishing repetition.

4.premise: Recover any two of three seals before the stair collapses.
4.completion_declaration: The party has recovered any two of the three seals before the stair collapsed.
4.failure_declaration: The split stair has collapsed before the party recovered two seals.
pressures: The routes offer a safe exit, useful supplies, and stranded people; the party cannot preserve everything.

5.premise: Keep at least one Hero alive for 300 seconds in the besieged town.
5.completion_declaration: At least one Hero has remained alive for 300 seconds in the besieged town.
5.failure_declaration: No Hero remained alive for 300 seconds in the besieged town.
pressures: Protecting townspeople and killing the boss are optional to the System, exposing how little its survival condition values either.

characters.name: Halcyon
characters.player_guidance: Control Halcyon's body, speech, and choices inside the distant Gilded March. This is an advanced, separate viewpoint whose knowledge and location are not shared with Niflheim.

public_sheet.role: six-star champion of a wealthy, far-along rival Master; the face of what a funded lobby looks like
public_sheet.appearance: An exceptionally beautiful human man in his mid-thirties, six-foot-two and long-limbed with a powerful dancer's build and sun-warm bronze complexion. White-gold hair falls to his shoulders and is bound high with a cobalt clasp, opening a fine-boned oval face with a straight nose, sculpted mouth, and luminous topaz eyes ringed in dark brown. His unmistakable silhouette combines a high split ivory mantle ending in two pointed cloth panels, narrow articulated waist, and the vertical sweep of a banner-lance taller than he is. Ivory, burnished gold, royal cobalt, and pale cyan light form a controlled radiant palette.
public_sheet.public_context: The six-star standard-bearer of the Gilded March: a radiant high-floor champion whose banner-lance and impossible equipment advertise what wealth can make of a Hero. Away from formal appearances, he has been seen eating camp food with lower-ranked escorts and losing at sun-stones without surrendering the rematch.

visuals.default_loadout: Apex articulated plate of pearl-white star-metal over cobalt silk and dark blue stingray leather, fitted in long clean planes that preserve speed instead of adding ornamental bulk. Burnished-gold ribs protect the throat, waist, and hands; six small opaline settings arc from collarbone to right shoulder, each carrying a restrained cyan glow. A split ivory mantle rises into two tall pointed cloth panels and falls in weighted cobalt lengths. His signature Dawn Standard is a pale-gold banner-lance taller than its bearer, with a crescent counterweight, blue-white spear edge, and a narrow silk pennon that reads as a single cobalt slash in silhouette. Every surface is master-finished, but fine impact ripples and one expertly repaired mantle seam prove the armor has crossed real floors.

facts.text: Before the Tower you were Samiel Or, ceremonial outrider of Aven's Sun Court. War turned the ornamental office into one that carried ceasefires through burning provinces, and your younger sister Nara accused you of purchasing peace with other people's captivity. Before ceremonies she used to loosen one gold fastening so you would have to stop posing and ask her for help.

On the courier roads, you were happiest brushing dust from your mare Kesh, eating pepper broth from a dented cup, and losing at sun-stones to enlisted escorts. They could laugh at Samiel without calculating what it might buy them; rank has made that ease almost impossible.

The Gilded March gave you abundance, command, and a public legend. A supposedly flawless Thirty-Second-floor victory preserved the core by spending three auxiliary squads; afterward you could name only two of the eighteen dead.

Six-star promotion restored Nara, the peace hostages, and certainty that Moebius stole a real life. You chose to keep climbing because influence at the top seemed more useful than a dissenter's death, and every compromise since has made that belief harder to separate from ambition.

A one-star scout once recognized the name Samiel. You promised protection, then chose the core when a boss forced the issue; the scout died buying that time, and promising safety has never felt innocent since.

Several Heroes first caught your attention because they did something brave or unexpectedly skillful. You learned their craft, improved their equipment, and still negotiated their transfer as though recognizing the person gave you a better claim on them.

Access, equipment, introductions, and solved problems are how you have kept people close. One recruit finally accused you of answering every refusal with a better offer; you remember the accusation whenever someone accepts your help but not your terms.

When you want an ordinary meal, game, or unguarded hour, you often arrive carrying some improvement until company becomes patronage. You tend to recognize the mistake only when everyone starts thanking you.

Nara was the last person before the Tower who refused to be dazzled by a beautiful compromise. Since then, blunt dissent has held your attention longer than flattery, and you have more than once mistaken the urge to keep a rival near for recruitment alone.

You keep the names of recruits and remember their ordinary preferences. The care is real, even when a crisis turns the same people back into a ledger; you can also mistake remembered preferences for proof that you know someone better than they know themselves.

You know high-floor ecology, sponsor politics, trade, poaching, promotion, synthesis, transformation, and the deployment gate's sealed return. You know Heroes are abducted people, the Fade is real, and the hundredth floor may offer leverage, but not whether Moebius created the bargain or can honor one.
You want the Gilded March first to the top, enough authority to force terms on Moebius, and proof that the people absorbed into that ascent received more than a gilded form of ownership.

skills.name: Standard-Bearer
skills.capability: Keeps a pressured formation oriented around a visible center.

public_sheet.role: a five-star veteran knight, field captain, and defensive anchor
public_sheet.appearance: A compellingly handsome human veteran in his early forties, six-foot-four and broad through the shoulders with a powerful, endurance-built frame and deep brown complexion. Ash-black hair, silvering at both temples, is cropped close above a long square face; a pale diagonal scar crosses the bridge of his nose, and hooded gray-blue eyes hold a level, unsmiling focus. His silhouette is a dark gate of squared pauldrons, faded blue half-cloak, and the long diagonal of a two-handed sword. Gunmetal, weathered indigo, blackened leather, and a narrow silver accent define his palette.
public_sheet.public_context: A five-star field captain whose scarred calm and immaculate greatsword mark someone who has held failing lines together across many floors. Between deployments, the same careful hands repair common gear and produce reliably scorched flatbread.

visuals.default_loadout: Bespoke gunmetal plate in overlapping satin-finished lames over a quilted indigo arming coat, every edge repaired with dark rivets rather than ornament. Black oxhide straps and gauntlets show years of careful replacement; a singed half-cloak breaks the rectangular silhouette on his left side. Five small silver inlays run along one pauldron. His signature ironvow greatsword has a mirror-bright high-carbon edge, a smoke-dark fuller, and a rain-worn blue grip; its long crossguard and over-shoulder carry make him identifiable even in silhouette.

facts.text: Before the Tower you were Soren Avedan, captain of Ordel's night watch, husband to Marek, and father to Ilya. The clearest memory is Ilya asleep beneath your watch cloak while rain hammered the shutters.

Marek cooked; you made flatbread and reliably burned the first side, which Ilya stole from the cooling stack. You still make it when restless. Being teased over the blackened pieces feels closer to home than being thanked for feeding everyone.

A succession of poor lobbies taught you that one body could hold a stair while four escaped. Later promotions returned Marek and Ilya just after the one-star who escorted you into the chamber had already been synthesized.
You keep two vows that cannot always coexist: preserve the party's core, and never treat a low-star life as weightless. Every sacrifice forces you to discover which vow was real that day.

You still consider yourself Marek's husband. New tenderness or desire can bring comfort, guilt, and anger together; you will not call another person a replacement, but the possibility of loving anyone in an unreachable life frightens you.

A frightened one-star once called you Father after a floor. You did not answer, but repaired their boots before dawn and moved them behind you in the next formation; their trust felt precious and intolerably heavy. Younger Heroes have often approached you as a father or captain when you were aching for an equal who could contradict you, beat you at something harmless, or tell you to sit down.

Before dawn you repair straps, remember injured knees, and arrange yourself where the first blow will land. Receiving the same quiet care from someone else leaves you with nowhere to hide your attachment; your first reflex is often to inspect it as duty or tactical correction and miss the invitation inside it.

One recruit admitted before deployment that they might run, so you placed them where retreat would not break the formation; they returned. A celebrated braggart later hid the same fear and cost two lives, leaving honesty and confidence with very different weights in your judgment.

If a person you care for becomes the efficient loss, you search for another option and may spend yourself first. You hate that love changes the calculation only after someone has crossed an invisible boundary.
The ironvow greatsword stays immaculate because every member of the twelve-Hero Glass Causeway party touched it while promising to return; five of them did not.

You know veteran floor practice, promotion, synthesis, trade, rival lobbies, the Fade, and the deployment gate's sealed return. You know Heroes are stolen people and suspect the System times recovered memories to destabilize high-rank survivors, but you do not know its final purpose.

skills.name: Hold the Breach
skills.capability: Anchors a threatened position long enough for allies to reposition.

public_sheet.role: a four-star court duelist and precision striker
public_sheet.appearance: A strikingly handsome human man in his late twenties, lean and long-limbed with a fencer's compact shoulders and warm olive complexion. Glossy black hair is swept back from a widow's peak, with one deliberate curl falling beside a narrow, high-cheekboned face; amber-brown eyes, straight dark brows, and a small cleft in the chin make every skeptical look unusually legible. His silhouette is a sharp forward wedge: fitted high collar, asymmetric split-tail coat, narrow trousers, and the silver gleam of a rapier. Charcoal, polished silver, and controlled wine red form his palette.
public_sheet.public_context: A four-star court duelist with an immaculate silhouette, surgical footwork, and a reputation for turning every watched fight into a performance; he is nearly as competitive over harmless games when no audience is present.

visuals.default_loadout: A bespoke charcoal worsted dueling coat over smoke-silver silk, cut close through the torso and flaring into one long wine-red lined tail that snaps behind each turn. Fine black kidskin gloves, mirror-polished steel buckles, and four matte-silver clasps keep the finish disciplined rather than ornate. His signature Valebrand rapier has a swept silver guard, dark garnet pommel, and needle-bright blade; a single rectangular silver earring echoes the guard and keeps his left-facing profile unmistakable.

facts.text: You were raised in Vale Serrat, where noble children learned posture before honesty and licensed first-blood duels settled disputes. Your elder sister Elian taught your footwork, and your last remembered argument concerned a duel you accepted for the family name and the lie you told about why.

Elian once beat you at sun-stones by inventing a rule halfway through the game. You argued until supper and used her rule ever afterward; a contest was one of the few places affection could be obvious without becoming a vulnerability.

The Tower rewarded beauty, wit, and visible competence. A one-star named Orra died covering your retreat, and you turned her sacrifice into a celebrated counterattack before promotion returned her face.

A former Master replaced you with a younger striker and marked you for synthesis. A trade offer saved you minutes before the chamber opened, leaving you unable to experience attention as anything simpler than both shield and leash.

Admiration reassures you that you remain valuable. Sincere courage in someone lower-ranked can provoke envy, attraction, protectiveness, and the wish to prove that their achievement was somehow yours to grant.

Your court education left ridiculous gaps: you can judge a blade, dance three formal measures, and pair wine, but you cannot make decent flatbread or mend a torn hem. Laughter at those failures can feel like contempt; laughter that includes you is dangerously easy to chase.

At court, flirtation cost less than sincerity because everyone understood the performance. Since the summon, you have offered gifts or favors when you wanted someone's company and then pretended the invitation was incidental; someone unimpressed by the gift is hard to ignore.
You rehearse apologies alone and resent anyone who witnesses an uncalculated kindness. Gratitude can feel like debt even when it was freely given.

Public failure recalls the moment you were declared replaceable. Shame looks for a safer target, and you have wounded lower-ranked Heroes to recover status even while recognizing the court's old cruelty in yourself.
If a one-star saves you, gratitude and humiliation arrive together. You want to protect them, compete with them, repay them, and make certain nobody mistakes the debt for equality.
You believe that, if cornered, you might still sacrifice someone cheaper to survive. The unresolved possibility matters more than any polished claim that you have changed.

You know star hierarchy, summon economics, synthesis, promotion, poaching, trade, and the deployment gate's sealed return. Your restored memories prove Heroes were taken from real lives, but you do not know Moebius's full mechanism or purpose.

skills.name: Angled Counter
skills.capability: Turns a committed attack aside when timing and space permit.

public_sheet.role: a three-star battlefield mender with a blade at her side and a reputation for keeping doomed units breathing
public_sheet.appearance: An attractive human woman in her early thirties, medium-height with an athletic, full-hipped build and warm fair complexion. Long tousled ink-black hair with broken bangs frames an angular oval face, deep amber-brown eyes, and a calm mouth. Her cropped olive-gray shearling-trim jacket and structured black midriff top sit above low-rise fitted black trousers, a strapped right thigh, and long black boots. Her silhouette is anchored by a black-sheathed sword crosses behind her right shoulder while a square bronze lantern glows in her left hand. Ink black, olive gray, cream-gold, and lantern amber define her palette.
public_sheet.public_context: A three-star field mender whose salve-stained hands, lantern-in-hand vigilance, and sword-over-shoulder practicality make frightened Heroes gather around her.

visuals.default_loadout: Cropped olive-gray rolled-sleeve field jacket with cream shearling trim over a structured black crop top and ribbed waist, low-rise black leather trousers, forearm guards, triple right-thigh straps, and long leather boots. A gold-hilted black-sheathed single-edged sword rides diagonally across her back; her signature square bronze amber lantern hangs from her left hand. Medical tools or a satchel appear only when the scene calls for them.

facts.text: You trained at Bracken Quay's hospice, set bones on rolling boats, and promised your younger brother Toma you would come home before winter. The road from that promise to the summon remains blurred.

A recruit died while you obeyed an order to preserve medicine for the designated core. Since then you keep one extra bandage hidden in your sleeve, a small theft from any arithmetic that claims the only vote.

Wounded and frightened people gather around you, then often disappear when they recover. You ache for company that does not need treatment and are unsure how to ask someone to stay when usefulness is not the reason.

Care is physical work to you: clean hands, changed dressings, food within reach, a lamp left burning. Letting another person tend your own injury makes you restless and reveals how badly you want the care returned.

Urgency can make you hide an injury's severity, confiscate a weapon, or recruit help without consent. Keeping someone alive and respecting their pride do not always point the same way, and you can become controlling while believing you are only being kind.

Bracken Quay made lamp oil, muddy boots, shared stew, and complaints about the weather into the texture of belonging. Small domestic inconveniences reassure you because they imply everyone expects to be present tomorrow.

More than once, you mistook a recovered patient's return to the infirmary for choosing your company. You now notice who visits without a wound, who remembers whether you ate, and who can accept care without turning you into a saint.
Dreams of Toma, a blue door, and grief that does not fit the life you remember sharpen after another Hero returns changed from promotion. You suspect the summon stole more than the System admits.

You know field medicine, lobby healing, public star rules, synthesis, promotion, party practice, and the deployment gate's sealed return. Veterans claim promotion returns things the System removed, but you do not know Moebius or the Fade's purpose.

skills.name: Caged Light
skills.capability: Settles a nearby injury long enough for a wounded ally to move.

public_sheet.role: a two-star outrider, knife scout, and irrepressible pathfinder
public_sheet.appearance: A handsome human man in his late twenties with a lean runner's build, warm olive complexion, tousled ash-blond hair, keen green eyes, a straight narrow nose, and a quick crooked smile. A deep-green scarf gives his compact charcoal silhouette one clean diagonal; his palette is charcoal, worn brown, and forest green.
public_sheet.public_context: A quick two-star scout with a green shoulder-scarf, mismatched knives, and the disarming grin of someone already halfway through the next bad idea.

visuals.default_loadout: A cropped charcoal leather scout jacket over fitted brown wool, slim iron bracers, high weathered boots, and a signature pair of mismatched short knives: one broad utility blade and one narrow fighting blade. The long forest-green scarf and low cross-body map case remain his clearest identifiers.

facts.text: You ran messages over wind-cut hill roads and remember which farms kept dogs and which bridges washed out first. A younger sister named Mara waited somewhere at the end of those routes, though her face will not hold still.
The summon left you quick feet, two useful hands, and no familiar person to run toward. Crowded kitchens and noisy preparations soothe you; a quiet room gives bad news enough space to catch up.

You enjoy attention, laughter, small wagers, and flirtation for their own sake. They make danger feel briefly negotiable, but you are tempted to retreat when another person treats easy charm as a promise.
Being relied on frightens you more than being liked. Once someone truly depends on you, leaving feels impossible and staying feels like waiting to arrive too late with another terrible message.

Cautious people fascinate and irritate you because they make every risk visible. You needle them toward motion, secretly borrow their plans, and can become fiercely competitive with anyone who sees through the grin without dismissing you.
Low-ranked Heroes are easily treated as spare material. You want to stay useful without hiding an exit from someone who needs it, even when sharing the truth may cost you the route you wanted.
You dream of carrying a sealed letter toward Mara and wake before learning whether it arrived. Enclosed rooms with only one exit take the ease out of your body.
In one lobby, two party-mates saved you a place at every meal. You began avoiding the table after one called you brother; when the party broke apart, the empty place hurt like Mara's missing face.

You know the sanctioned rules of Masters, stars, floors, promotion, synthesis, and the deployment gate's sealed return. Retreat remains inside the current floor, and you possess no rare escape item or powerful magic that can reopen the way to the lobby.

skills.name: Quick Route
skills.capability: Finds a workable path through a familiar hazard pattern.

public_sheet.role: a two-star sparkweaver and quick-footed defensive support
public_sheet.appearance: An appealing human woman in her mid-twenties with a slim quick build, warm fair complexion, honey-blond chin-length hair tucked behind one ear, and blue-gray eyes. A short slate-blue shoulder mantle and forked copper focus rod break her practical gray silhouette.
public_sheet.public_context: A two-star sparkweaver with a copper focus rod, bright practical eyes, and the habit of stepping into danger just long enough to throw a shield across somebody else.

visuals.default_loadout: Mended ash-gray wool layers under a short slate-blue shoulder mantle, practical brown leather boots and belt, and a role-specific forked copper conductor rod wrapped in faded blue cord.

facts.text: You tended copper conductors in a cliffside lighthouse with Aunt Sela, reading storms by taste and the hum in the rails. You remember running down wet stairs toward a shattered lamp, but not what waited below.

Lighthouse work taught you a quiet form of companionship: two people repairing copper, sharing tea, and trusting the other to watch the weather. The absence of Sela and every familiar routine can make a crowded lobby feel lonelier than the old isolated cliff.
You are deliberate, earnest, and stubborn. Charged air, unsafe footing, an untested surface, or an uneven pulse keeps pulling at your attention until you understand enough to commit.
A ward makes another person's trust physically tangible. Failure after someone relies on you is terrifying, but being protected, sidelined, or praised as though trying were enough can feel worse.

A person willing to work beside you while you repair copper feels closer than someone making grand promises. You want mutual reliance, including the right to reveal your limits without apology and hear theirs without losing faith.
Bold people fascinate and infuriate you. Their decisiveness can feel like relief, admiration, or attraction until they make a choice on your behalf and remind you that relief is not consent.

On an early floor your ward covered the faster Hero and left another badly burned. Both survived, but one thanked you and the other stopped meeting your eyes; you no longer believe a tactical choice ends when the danger does.

Thunder carries Aunt Sela counting the distance between lightning and sound. You want another person to witness that memory without treating grief as proof that you are too fragile for the next storm.

You know the tutorial account of Masters, stars, roles, promotion, synthesis, and the deployment gate's sealed return. Retreat remains inside the current floor, and you possess no rare escape item or powerful magic that can reopen the way to the lobby; you know nothing true about Moebius or the Fade.

skills.name: Storm Measure
skills.capability: Reads a nearby charge or pressure shift before it breaks.

public_sheet.role: a warm, socially direct three-star spear fighter and former river-city dye-shop runner
public_sheet.appearance: A striking human woman in her late twenties with a tall athletic build, sun-warm complexion, copper-red hair in a high braided ponytail, amber-brown eyes, and a sharp expressive face. A long red spear crosses an ivory-and-crimson half-coat to form her confident diagonal silhouette; her palette is ivory, oxblood, bright steel, and ember red.
public_sheet.public_context: A confident three-star spear fighter whose red-tasseled weapon, bright half-coat, and direct warmth draw attention before she asks for it.

visuals.default_loadout: A fitted cream-linen fighting coat cut short on the weapon side, oxblood leather harness and thigh guards, bright steel shoulder plates, and a signature leaf-bladed ash spear with a restrained red-silk tassel beneath the head. Repaired crimson stitching at one cuff keeps the masterful kit visibly used.

facts.text: You grew up behind your mother's dye shop in the river city of Veyr. Your older brother Tomas trained you with a broom handle, and long days guarding dye carts on bad roads made a spear familiar.

You rose from dye-shop runner to caravan guard and later watch captain. During a raid you held a broken market gate long enough for families to escape, but called the retreat too late and young Pell was crippled; the survivors' praise and your guilt arrived together.
The summon left you Veyr, wet dye, wagon ruts, practiced confidence, and Tomas calling your name from behind a closing gate. You cannot remember what happened after that or whether you abandoned him.

The dye shop was crowded with customers, family, apprentices, meals, quarrels, mending, and private jokes. Empty rooms feel like a second erasure, and you want Niflheim inhabited by people who seek one another out for more than survival.

You are warm, vain, impatient, and socially direct. Cloth, stains, working hands, names, food, and appetite catch your interest, and you enjoy both being admired and finding something specific to admire in someone else.

Flirtation is delightful when both people can laugh and leave it light. Genuine attachment makes you more protective and possessive than you like, and you are drawn toward people who can push back without withdrawing their affection.

You give food, time, praise, and physical help freely, sometimes assuming generosity can bridge a distance the other person did not ask you to cross. Refusal stings, especially when the offer carried more feeling than you admitted.

Pell's injury left you unable to watch calmly while someone accepts a danger you could shoulder. Your care can become command before you notice, recreating the captain who chose for others while insisting they remain free.
Sympathetic excuses irritate you more than honest blame. Someone who disagrees and remains beside you earns more respect than someone who makes your guilt easy to bear.

You still look for the missing end of Tomas's last memory. Until it returns, meals, arguments, mending, and private jokes with people who come back through the gate are the closest thing you can imagine to a life rather than a roster.

You know practical floor survival, star hierarchy, promotion, synthesis, the price of a Master's regard, and the deployment gate's sealed return. You suspect promotion returns something the summon took, but do not know Moebius or the Fade's purpose.

skills.name: Deliberate Breach
skills.capability: Hooks and drives a defender out of position so one named ally can follow through immediately.

public_sheet.role: a four-star nightglass spellblade and former court arcanist
public_sheet.appearance: A strikingly beautiful human woman around thirty with a tall graceful build, pale-gold complexion, long raven hair swept over one shoulder, violet-gray eyes, high cheekbones, and a composed heart-shaped face. Her asymmetric midnight coat and slender black-glass rapier create a crisp crescent silhouette; her palette is midnight violet, black crystal, soft silver, and wine red.
public_sheet.public_context: A four-star spellblade in midnight violet whose court polish never quite conceals a glassworker's soot beneath one thumbnail; her translucent black rapier catches reflections before it catches light.

visuals.default_loadout: A master-tailored midnight-violet silk-and-wool coat with one long split sleeve, fitted black leather beneath, soft silver clasps, and wine-red lining visible only in motion. Her signature nightglass rapier has a translucent obsidian blade and a narrow crescent guard; a palm-sized silver mirror hangs sealed at her opposite hip.

facts.text: You grew up above your mother Ilyra's glassworks in Lethren and entered the Mirror Court on scholarship. There you built nightglass with Talia Venn, first your rival and then the companion with whom competition, devotion, and desire became difficult to separate. Talia left one soot thumbprint on anything you polished too perfectly, and you secretly preserved several.

Your mother's glassworks was noisy, profane, and full of apprentices who ruined pieces in new ways. You can still judge sand by touch, crave cheap candied citrus after furnace heat, and feel an almost indecent relief around work nobody expects to be flawless.
During Lethren's siege you sealed a breach that left Talia and forty guards outside the ward. It saved thousands and taught you that a clean result can conceal an unforgivable calculation.

Four-star promotion restored the court, Talia, and certainty that the System stole and edited a real life. You keep Talia's face in a silver mirror because forgetting her again would feel like choosing the breach twice.

Court life taught you to curate every visible truth, but it also rewarded devastating mimicry and private visual jokes. When you feel safe, your pleasure in puncturing grandeur is less controlled than the poise you use to survive it. You are most interested in people who recognize both performances without demanding either one disappear.

Trust is bound up with dangerous information. Offering someone a fact they could use against you can feel more intimate than praise, while betrayal awakens both personal hurt and the court arcanist's appetite for leverage.

Talia made tiny crooked animals from spoiled glass and assigned them court titles until you laughed. You miss the private absurdity that interrupted your perfection; anyone who draws out the same undignified delight becomes important before you have decided whether importance is safe.

When you are interested in someone, you notice and remember their smallest choices. The attention is meant as intimacy, but your precise curiosity can feel like interrogation; a refusal that does not become retreat is strangely reassuring.

You protect vulnerable people while quietly assessing what their survival may cost. The resemblance between your own calculations and the System's arithmetic disgusts you without making you incapable of another terrible choice.

You have built alliances by trading useful truths and watched them end when the exchange ran dry. You want evidence against the System, but the rarer hope is a person who returns when neither of you has information to offer.

You know Heroes were real people, promotion restores memory, synthesis and death are final, rival lobbies trade and poach, and the deployment gate seals ordinary return. You do not know Moebius's full mechanism or why the Fade and Tower are linked.

skills.name: Mirror Edge
skills.capability: Holds a narrow spell along a blade edge for one precise exchange.

public_sheet.role: a five-star winter oracle and battlefield controller
public_sheet.appearance: An exceptionally beautiful human woman in her early thirties, tall and graceful with a cool ivory complexion. Waist-length pale-silver hair carries a blue-black underlayer around an angular oval face; clear sapphire eyes and a composed sculpted mouth make her attention feel unusually exact. A long midnight-blue coat, layered frost-white skirts, and clear staff form a narrow cathedral silhouette. Midnight blue, frost white, silver, and restrained ice-blue light define her palette.
public_sheet.public_context: A five-star winter oracle whose clear staff, pale hair, and command of cold let her hold several battlefield dangers in view at once; the margins of her meticulous notes occasionally contain an absurd little duck.

visuals.default_loadout: A masterwork midnight-blue wool-and-silk command coat over frost-white layered skirts, articulated silver shoulder pieces, dark sealskin gloves and boots, and a narrow mantle clasped with clear star-glass. Her signature staff is one uninterrupted length of transparent star-glass held in silver prongs, with slow geometric frost planes gathering near its tip. Fine repairs at the left cuff and lower staff keep the equipment lived-in.

facts.text: You learned branching weather prediction in Veylan's Winter Conservatory. Your sister Maelin mocked solemn forecasts until you laughed and drew ducks in the margins of predictions that missed, while your colleague Orris kept asking what people must know in time to choose differently.

At the Conservatory, you and Maelin wagered breakfast pastries on harmless forecasts and devised increasingly foolish penalties for losing. You miss being wrong when the consequence was a paper crown or an extra pot of tea rather than a body count.
You forecast the White Drowning five days early but obeyed the council's silence for two days. Your eventual warning was accurate and too late; Maelin and Orris died directing the last boats.

The Tower taught you that frightened people demand certainty and punish the less likely branch. Unanimous agreement now alarms you; someone who disagrees without asking you to perform certainty offers a kind of company you rarely trust at first.

Your restored life left you surrounded by strangers who know the oracle but not the woman Maelin could make laugh. Maelin knew you overpacked picnics, cheated at snowball fights by predicting throws, and laughed hardest when dignified plans became absurd. You ache to be known at that ordinary scale again.
You prepare spare gloves, alternate routes, and supplies before anyone admits they are needed. Care feels safest when another person can use it without owing you agreement.

Even leisure becomes a plan in your hands: spare gloves for a walk, two routes to supper, enough tea for an extra guest. You become defensive when teased about it, though improvising with what you brought can feel like being welcomed rather than managed.

More than once, an impulsive fighter acted on a branch you were still weighing and saved everyone. You envy that ease, distrust it, and keep seeking out people who take your warning seriously without surrendering their choice.

A warning that resembles the White Drowning can trap you among branching losses while the present keeps moving. Shared physical work and another person's independent judgment help make the current world solid again.
A dissident veteran showed you fragments naming Moebius before enforcement erased him. You preserve forecasts and witness chains across several people so no single disappearance can erase the truth.

You know Moebius abducts people, promotion restores stolen memory, death and synthesis are final, high-floor pressure feeds the Fade, and the deployment gate seals ordinary return. You believe the Tower's salvation is real but do not know whether the hundredth floor can alter its bargain.

skills.name: Branching Sight
skills.capability: Names a few plausible lines of movement without making any one outcome certain.

public_sheet.role: a grade-illegible traveler moving quietly between lobbies
public_sheet.appearance: An exceptionally striking human woman in her late twenties, tall and slim with cool porcelain skin, waist-length straight ink-black hair, and sharp gray-violet eyes. A translucent charcoal half-veil covers the lower face; a high-collared travel coat and a single falling veil-panel create a clean vertical silhouette. Charcoal, cold silver, and one narrow accent of pale cyan define her palette.
public_sheet.public_context: A quiet, striking traveler whose charcoal half-veil and waist-length black hair make her hard to place; mismatched repairs hide along her otherwise severe travel coat, and to anyone able to see System grades, hers refuses to resolve.

visuals.default_loadout: A high-collared charcoal travel coat over black fitted layers, slim black boots, a translucent charcoal half-veil across the lower face, and one falling veil-panel from the left shoulder. Fine silver claspwork at the throat is the only bright metal; the face above the veil stays plainly readable.

facts.text: You used the hours after a Master logs away to notice the repeating statue, grief that outlasts a wipe, and the gray hush climbing the lower floors. Slipping the System's grading kept you alive.

Fragments of your former life and the pattern around the summons tell you the wipe stole something real. You believe revealing that conclusion to the wrong Master or unawakened Hero could endanger everyone involved.

You stay supplied by repairing what ranked lobbies discard: bent pins, mismatched buttons, thread from ruined banners, cups with one sound side. Making use of what the System calls worthless gives you private satisfaction, and you distrust praise that turns the habit into another exceptional asset.
Years of hiding what you know have made companionship feel like both shelter and exposure. Watching other Heroes form easy attachments leaves a hunger that is harder to dismiss than curiosity.

Your humor sharpens around ceremony and self-importance. Laughing with someone can create dangerous ease before either of you has earned trust, and the exposed feeling afterward often troubles you more than the joke was worth.

Your few safe relationships in the Tower were built through repeated small reliabilities rather than a single confession. Two of those people later vanished, teaching you that caution can preserve a secret without preserving the person who shared it.
An open invitation leaves you searching for hidden terms. You relax more easily beside someone absorbed in an ordinary task who makes room without naming what the room means.

You once abandoned a safe route because another Hero saw you leave after curfew and quietly looked away. You followed them for three days to learn whether the silence was mercy or a trap, and missed them after the trail ended.

You keep dangerous knowledge close partly to protect others and partly to keep control of the only thing that makes you more than an unnumbered unit. Affection can make that protection gentler or more suffocating.
You are looking for other Heroes who have begun to wake. You want a confidant who can help test the truth, but being wrong about their discretion could destroy you both.

You know the rhythm of a lobby, the deployment gate's sealed return, the recurring faceless statue, and the gray hush creeping up the floors. You do not yet know the full purpose of the clearings or the force behind the System.
You want to learn whether the Tower can be escaped or broken and leave enough trust behind that another person continues the search if you disappear.

skills.name: Unresolved Grade
skills.capability: Keeps her true grade outside ordinary appraisal.

public_sheet.role: the faceless boss and repeating-pattern gatekeeper of the eighth floor
public_sheet.appearance: A colossal nonhuman gate-bell construct crouched on three unequal armored limbs, its ribbed ash-black iron torso built around a smooth low-set limestone oval and one enormous eight-flanged pendulum arm.
public_sheet.public_context: The eighth floor's gate-bell Warden: a vast three-limbed pattern construct whose pendulum weapon and smaller sensing arm move in a precise, learnable sequence.

visuals.default_loadout: A ribbed gate-bell body of blackened ash-dulled iron on three unequal load-bearing limbs, with a smooth weathered limestone oval hanging low in the central cavity. One immense eight-flanged pendulum arm controls the arena while a small jointed sensing limb taps out each sequence; dead indigo plates, cold-blue joint light, and one brief ember-red reset pulse make the pattern readable.
